puzzles.name: Salt Barrel of the Bridgewater Triangle
puzzles.subtitle: Salem Sound

entry.title: SALT BARREL OF THE BRIDGEWATER TRIANGLE · CASE 001
entry.body: One Salt Barrel of the Bridgewater Triangle, recovered at Cape Ann. No owner came forward. Per policy, unclaimed evidence is destroyed after ninety days. This item has been in storage since 1911.

entry.title: EYESHINE OF THE BRIDGEWATER TRIANGLE · CASE 002
entry.body: It was just sitting there, out past the Breakwater, like it had been left for someone to find. Maybe it was. Maybe that someone was me.

entry.title: THE SEVERED TENTACLE · CASE 003
entry.body: The Severed Tentacle was delivered to the society in 1903 by a farmer who would accept no payment, wishing only to be rid of it.

entry.title: THE BARNACLED FISH BONES · CASE 004
entry.body: The Barnacled Fish Bones was catalogued, photographed, and locked up. The lock has needed replacing twice. No further comment is on record.

entry.title: THE WEATHERED MOORING CLEAT · CASE 005
entry.body: My uncle kept it in a drawer since 1854. Would not say where he got it. After he passed, I found the map it was wrapped in.

entry.title: THE SPYGLASS · CASE 006
entry.body: Recovered upon the road past Hockomock Swamp in the year 1931: this curious article, of which no traveller would claim ownership. It is set down here among the evidence.

entry.title: THE TRIDENT · CASE 007
entry.body: I found it half-covered near Provincetown Spit. Nobody camps out there. Nobody has for years. I brought it back and I still wish I had not.

entry.title: THE SALT-CRUSTED DECK CANNON · CASE 008
entry.body: My uncle kept it in a drawer since 1852. Would not say where he got it. After he passed, I found the map it was wrapped in.

entry.title: THE HANDPRINT · CASE 009
entry.body: Item logged 1979. Chain of custody: incomplete. Explanation on file: none. Status: unresolved, like the rest of the drawer.

entry.title: THE BREAKING WAVE · CASE 010
entry.body: Field note: passed the Breaking Wave twice on the same trail, walking the same direction. The compass agreed with me. My legs did not.

entry.title: THE LOBSTER TRAP · CASE 011
entry.body: Found at the Fog Banks: one The Lobster Trap, owner unknown. No tracks leading in. No tracks leading out. Logged and shelved.

entry.title: BITE MARK OF PROVINCETOWN SPIT · CASE 012
entry.body: Field note: item recovered off the trail past Salem Sound. Condition inconsistent with time exposed. Recommend cross-reference with prior cases.

entry.title: HARPOON OF SALEM SOUND · CASE 013
entry.body: Let this entry attest that the article was found at Lake Champlain, untouched by weather in a season of storms. Philosophy offers no account of it.

entry.title: THE BLUE MUSSEL · CASE 014
entry.body: It was 1986 and I swore I would never tell anyone. But I know what stood at the edge of Lake Champlain, and it was no animal I can name.

entry.title: THE QUAHOG CLAM · CASE 015
entry.body: I found it half-covered near Dover. Nobody camps out there. Nobody has for years. I brought it back and I still wish I had not.

entry.title: THE DORY · CASE 016
entry.body: Recovered near the Breakwater, 1889. Bagged, tagged, photographed. Nothing about where it lay makes sense. The file stays open.

entry.title: THE SLICK HARBOR PORPOISE · CASE 017
entry.body: Sighted near the Breakwater, 1957. Held still at the tree line, then was gone. Tracks pressed deep in wet ground. Recommend the file stay open.

entry.title: THE MESSAGE IN A BOTTLE · CASE 018
entry.body: One The Message in a Bottle, recovered at Dover. No owner came forward. Per policy, unclaimed evidence is destroyed after ninety days. This item has been in storage since 1889.

entry.title: THE HARBOR SEAL · CASE 019
entry.body: Second-hand account, Salem Sound, 1940. Consistent with prior The Harbor Seal reports — same height, same silence. Cross-reference earlier cases.

entry.title: THE WEATHERED OAR · CASE 020
entry.body: Let this entry attest that the article was found at Gloucester Harbor, untouched by weather in a season of storms. Philosophy offers no account of it.

puzzles.name: Atlantic Cod of the Bridgewater Triangle
puzzles.subtitle: Salem Sound

entry.title: ATLANTIC COD OF THE BRIDGEWATER TRIANGLE · CASE 021
entry.body: Sighted near Salem Sound, 1986. Held still at the tree line, then was gone. Tracks pressed deep in wet ground. Recommend the file stay open.

entry.title: SNAPPING TURTLE OF LAKE CHAMPLAIN · CASE 022
entry.body: The guide would not speak its name above a whisper. Near the Fog Banks we beheld the Snapping Turtle of Lake Champlain, and no man among us slept that night.

entry.title: THE PALE ATLANTIC PUFFIN · CASE 023
entry.body: Duration of sighting: under a minute. Location: Cape Ann. Conclusion: inconclusive, which is the only honest word for it.

entry.title: THE WEATHERED WHALE-OIL LAMP · CASE 024
entry.body: Field note: item recovered off the trail past Salem Sound. Condition inconsistent with time exposed. Recommend cross-reference with prior cases.

entry.title: THE LIGHTHOUSE · CASE 025
entry.body: We used to dare each other to touch the Lighthouse when we were kids. The dare was easy. It was the walk back nobody talked about.

entry.title: THE SALTBOX HOUSE · CASE 026
entry.body: The Saltbox House was photographed for the record. The record now has a photograph of the Fog Banks with nothing in it. Both are filed.

entry.title: WHALE WEATHERVANE OF THE BREAKWATER · CASE 027
entry.body: Surveyed Gloucester Harbor, 1961. The Whale Weathervane of the Breakwater is on no map of the area, and the county keeps no record of it. It is there all the same.

entry.title: CONCH SHELL OF THE BREAKWATER · CASE 028
entry.body: Recovered upon the road past Cape Ann in the year 1985: this curious article, of which no traveller would claim ownership. It is set down here among the evidence.

entry.title: THE CORMORANT · CASE 029
entry.body: We were near Gloucester Harbor when the dogs quit barking all at once. That is when I saw it. I have not been back after dark since.

entry.title: SAND DOLLAR OF THE BREAKWATER · CASE 030
entry.body: It was just sitting there, out past Lake Champlain, like it had been left for someone to find. Maybe it was. Maybe that someone was me.

entry.title: THE CHURCH STEEPLE · CASE 031
entry.body: Locals will not camp within sight of the Church Steeple. When asked why, they answer a different question. Noted, 1881; still unexplained.

entry.title: THE WEATHERED ANCHOR · CASE 032
entry.body: Let this entry attest that the article was found at the Bridgewater Triangle, untouched by weather in a season of storms. Philosophy offers no account of it.

entry.title: THE ATLANTIC BLUE CRAB · CASE 033
entry.body: Duration of sighting: under a minute. Location: the Fog Banks. Conclusion: inconclusive, which is the only honest word for it.

entry.title: THE ANCIENT ATLANTIC COD · CASE 034
entry.body: Field note: heavy sign along Provincetown Spit. Snapped branches at eight feet. Smell of wet copper. Did not linger to confirm.

entry.title: THE COILING HARBOR SEAL · CASE 035
entry.body: Observed 1856 near the Fog Banks. Approximately human height, not human gait. No further comment was offered by the witness or requested of them.

entry.title: WOOD DEVIL OF DOVER · CASE 036
entry.body: Our party, encamped near Cape Ann in the autumn of 1908, observed a figure of uncommon stature. It regarded us without fear, then withdrew as though it had never been.

entry.title: THE COILING FOG WALKER · CASE 037
entry.body: Observed 1831 near Hockomock Swamp. Approximately human height, not human gait. No further comment was offered by the witness or requested of them.

puzzles.name: Great Blue Heron of Salem Sound
puzzles.subtitle: Lake Champlain

entry.title: GREAT BLUE HERON OF SALEM SOUND · CASE 038
entry.body: We were near Lake Champlain when the dogs quit barking all at once. That is when I saw it. I have not been back after dark since.

entry.title: THE WHALING DORY · CASE 039
entry.body: We found the Whaling Dory on the second day. Whatever left it there had come back through Gloucester Harbor that same night. The prints went right past our tent.

entry.title: THE COILING CORMORANT · CASE 040
entry.body: Duration of sighting: under a minute. Location: Hockomock Swamp. Conclusion: inconclusive, which is the only honest word for it.

entry.title: MOOSE OF PROVINCETOWN SPIT · CASE 041
entry.body: It was 1904 and I swore I would never tell anyone. But I know what stood at the edge of the Bridgewater Triangle, and it was no animal I can name.

entry.title: THE TIDE-WORN PUKWUDGIE · CASE 042
entry.body: The guide would not speak its name above a whisper. Near the Breakwater we beheld the Tide-Worn Pukwudgie, and no man among us slept that night.

entry.title: HUMPBACK WHALE OF PROVINCETOWN SPIT · CASE 043
entry.body: I only saw it for a breath, out past Cape Ann. It watched me the way a person watches, then stepped back into the dark and was just gone.

entry.title: THE SALT-CRUSTED GLAWACKUS · CASE 044
entry.body: Duration of sighting: under a minute. Location: Cape Ann. Conclusion: inconclusive, which is the only honest word for it.

entry.title: THE SLICK GLOUCESTER SEA SERPENT · CASE 045
entry.body: Our party, encamped near the Fog Banks in the autumn of 1962, observed a figure of uncommon stature. It regarded us without fear, then withdrew as though it had never been.

entry.title: THE SALT-CRUSTED LOBSTER BOAT · CASE 046
entry.body: Catalogued 1850. The Salt-Crusted Lobster Boat was exactly where the witness said it would be. That is the part that bothers me.

entry.title: CHAMP OF LAKE CHAMPLAIN · CASE 047
entry.body: Let the record show that on the road past the Bridgewater Triangle, in the year 1882, a thing was seen which philosophy cannot yet explain.

entry.title: THE LEATHERBACK TURTLE · CASE 048
entry.body: Field note: heavy sign along the Breakwater. Snapped branches at eight feet. Smell of wet copper. Did not linger to confirm.

entry.title: THE TIDE-WORN HUMPBACK WHALE · CASE 049
entry.body: We were near Provincetown Spit when the dogs quit barking all at once. That is when I saw it. I have not been back after dark since.

entry.title: THE WEATHERED SLOOP · CASE 050
entry.body: Our party came upon the Weathered Sloop near Lake Champlain, abandoned in circumstances I hesitate to record. We carried it out; none among us would carry it twice.

puzzles.name: Giant Octopus of the Fog Banks
puzzles.subtitle: Cape Ann

entry.title: GIANT OCTOPUS OF THE FOG BANKS · CASE 051
entry.body: A dark shape off the Breakwater. Three witnesses, one photograph, no clear resolution. The report was filed and, per policy, quietly closed.

entry.title: THE STORM-GREY CHAMP · CASE 052
entry.body: Sighted near the Bridgewater Triangle, 2002. Held still at the tree line, then was gone. Tracks pressed deep in wet ground. Recommend the file stay open.

entry.title: THUNDERBIRD OF GLOUCESTER HARBOR · CASE 053
entry.body: Sighted near the Breakwater, 1937. Held still at the tree line, then was gone. Tracks pressed deep in wet ground. Recommend the file stay open.

entry.title: THE HUMPBACK WHALE · CASE 054
entry.body: A dark shape off the Bridgewater Triangle. Three witnesses, one photograph, no clear resolution. The report was filed and, per policy, quietly closed.

entry.title: MOOSE OF LAKE CHAMPLAIN · CASE 055
entry.body: We were near Provincetown Spit when the dogs quit barking all at once. That is when I saw it. I have not been back after dark since.

entry.title: THE SEA SERPENT · CASE 056
entry.body: I set down this account of the Bridgewater Triangle that it may not be lost: a creature of the old accounts, thought a fable, stood not forty paces distant.

entry.title: THE SCHOONER · CASE 057
entry.body: Recovered near Cape Ann, 1978. Bagged, tagged, photographed. Nothing about where it lay makes sense. The file stays open.

entry.title: HUMPBACK WHALE OF THE BREAKWATER · CASE 058
entry.body: My grandfather saw it first. Now I have too, plain as day, out by Salem Sound. Whatever the Humpback Whale of the Breakwater is, it remembers this valley.

entry.title: THE STORM-LASHED LIGHTHOUSE · CASE 059
entry.body: The Storm-Lashed Lighthouse appears in three surveys and is absent from four. All seven were conducted competently. No further survey is planned.

entry.title: THE ANCIENT CHAMP · CASE 060
entry.body: We were near the Fog Banks when the dogs quit barking all at once. That is when I saw it. I have not been back after dark since.
